Functionality: GetOverviewAsync requires an authenticated tenant context and a run that exists in that tenant, else Unauthorized/NotFound
Overview aggregates persisted employee count and gross/deduction/net/employer-contribution/tax totals from current, Calculated PayrollResults only
Overview separately sums active (non-Cancelled) BankAdviceBatches.TotalAmount and active (non-Cancelled) PayrollJournalBatches debit/credit totals for the same run
Overview reports OpenFindings/CriticalFindings counts from PayrollReconciliationFindings with Status=Open (Critical additionally filtered by Severity=Critical)
Overview reports AnomalyCount from PayrollAnomalyFlags with Status=Open, scoped to the run

GetRunSummaryAsync returns run type/status plus the full PayrollControlTotalsDto and, when present, bank-advice/accounting debit/credit totals as nullable (null, not zero, when no active batch/journal exists)
GetControlTotalsAsync computes distinct-employee count, result count, and Earnings/Deduction/Gross/Net/EmployerContribution/Tax totals from persisted PayrollResults
Control totals derive Reimbursement/LoanRecovery/VariablePay/Adjustment sub-totals from PayrollResultComponents.CalculationSource via a case-insensitive substring match, not an exact enum/type match
Control totals' Tax field is always a hard-coded 0m (Totals() returns a fixed 0m for Tax regardless of persisted statutory data)
Both GetRunSummaryAsync and GetControlTotalsAsync require the run to resolve for the caller's tenant first, else the same NotFound/Unauthorized propagates
SummaryCsv and ControlTotalsCsv export the same computed values as their JSON counterparts as single-data-row CSV files with a UTF-8 BOM and RFC 4180 escaping
GetDepartmentSummaryAsync and GetCostCenterSummaryAsync join PayrollRunEmployees to current Calculated PayrollResults, grouping by the run-employee's own DepartmentId/CostCenterId
Department/CostCenter dimension ids and names are read from PayrollRunEmployee's own historical snapshot columns, never from the employee's current Department/CostCenter assignment
A null historical dimension groups together under a synthetic 'UNCLASSIFIED' code / 'Historical dimension unavailable' name row, rather than being dropped or erroring

A historical dimension id that no longer resolves to a live Department/CostCenter row (deleted/renamed since the run) still falls back to the same UNCLASSIFIED code/name pair rather than the dimension's own stale id
Dimension summary rows are ordered by Code ascending, with UNCLASSIFIED sorting per ordinary string comparison (no special-cased placement)

Each dimension row reports its own distinct-employee count, result count, and Earnings/Gross/Deduction/Net/EmployerContribution totals; the sum across all dimension rows reconciles exactly to the run's overall control totals

PayrollDimensionSummaryDto's EarningsTotal and GrossTotal are always equal for every row (both are populated from the same GrossEarnings sum) - there is no separate earnings-vs-gross distinction at the dimension level
Both dimension summary endpoints require the run to resolve for the caller's tenant first, else NotFound/Unauthorized
GetVarianceAsync computes a per-employee row comparing the requested run's current PayrollResult against a comparison run's prior PayrollResult, joined by EmployeeId

When compareRunId is omitted, the comparison run defaults to the most recent OTHER non-Cancelled run of the SAME RunType for the tenant, ordered by PayrollPeriod.EndDate descending - regardless of that run's own Status (Draft/Prepared/Processing all qualify, not just Calculated+)
An explicit compareRunId is used as-is with no validation that it belongs to the same tenant, the same RunType, or resolves to any PayrollResults at all

An employee present in the current run but absent from the comparison run's results is classified Classification=NewValue with null Base* fields; GrossDelta/DeductionDelta/NetDelta are computed against an implicit 0 prior
Percent() returns null (not an error, not Infinity) when the prior/base value is exactly zero, and rounds to 6 decimal places otherwise
Free-text search on the variance list matches EmployeeCode or EmployeeName case-insensitively, applied AFTER the full current-run/comparison-run join is materialized in memory (not pushed to SQL)
The variance list is always ordered by EmployeeCode ascending and paged with the shared PagedQuery Page/PageSize (default 20, max 100), independent of any SortBy value supplied

PayrollVarianceRowDto.Flags is always an empty array and Classification is always exactly one of the two literal strings NewValue/NormalComparable, never reflecting the magnitude of the computed variance percent (see CR-299)
VarianceCsv exports every matching row (PageSize forced to 50000 internally) with the same 15 columns as the JSON shape, RFC 4180 escaped, named payroll-variance-{runId:N}.csv
GetVarianceAsync requires the requested run to resolve for the caller's tenant first, else NotFound/Unauthorized (independent of whether compareRunId belongs to that tenant)
GetComponentVarianceAsync groups PayrollResultComponents by (CalculationSource, ComponentCode, ComponentName) for both the current and comparison run and sums CalculatedAmount per group
The result is a union of every distinct grouping key seen in EITHER run; a key present only in one run reports 0 for the other run's amount rather than being omitted
Component variance uses the identical default-comparison-run selection rule as employee variance (most recent other same-RunType non-Cancelled run) when compareRunId is omitted
Component variance is not paged (returns the full IReadOnlyList) and has no dedicated CSV export endpoint, unlike employee variance
GetComponentVarianceAsync requires the requested run to resolve for the caller's tenant first, else NotFound/Unauthorized
GenerateReconciliationAsync(PrePayroll) creates a new versioned PayrollReconciliation row, version = prior-max-version-for-this-type + 1 (1 if none exists)
Pre-payroll with zero persisted PayrollResults raises a single Critical, BlockApproval-tagged NoPayrollResults finding
Every reconciliation generation call (pre or post) also inserts exactly one PayrollAnalyticsSnapshot row capturing the persisted totals/employee count/currency at that DataVersion
GenerateReconciliationAsync requires the run to resolve for the caller's tenant first, else NotFound/Unauthorized, before any finding/snapshot is written
Post-payroll raises a Critical PayrollEquationMismatch finding whenever persisted Gross - Deductions <> Net (the equation is evaluated over already-persisted totals, never recomputed from components)
Post-payroll raises one Critical NegativeNetPay finding PER employee with NetPay < 0, and separately creates a PayrollAnomalyFlag(NegativeNetPay) for that employee if one is not already Open

Post-payroll raises one Warning ZeroNetPay finding (run-level, not per-employee) when the run's total Net = 0 AND at least one result exists, plus a matching PayrollAnomalyFlag(ZeroNetPay) if one is not already Open

Only effective-dated PayrollVarianceControls scoped to PayrollRun, active, whose EffectiveFrom<=period end<=EffectiveTo (or null), and whose AppliesToRunType matches (or is null), are evaluated; an out-of-window or inactive control is silently skipped

A matching run-level control whose |actual| exceeds either its AbsoluteThreshold or its PercentageThreshold (both checked against the same raw metric value, not scaled to a percent) raises a finding tagged with the control's own Code/Severity/Action/Metric
Post-payroll raises Warning MissingBankAdvice when persisted results exist but no active (non-Cancelled) BankAdviceBatch exists for the run
Post-payroll raises Critical BankAdviceAmountMismatch when the sum of active BankAdviceBatches.TotalAmount does not equal the run's persisted Net total
Post-payroll raises Warning BankAdviceCountMismatch when the count of active, non-Cancelled BankAdvicePayments does not equal the run's persisted result count
Post-payroll raises Critical DuplicateBankPaymentReference when 2+ active BankAdvicePayments for the run's batches share the same non-empty PaymentReference
Post-payroll raises Warning MissingPayrollJournal when persisted results exist but no active (non-Cancelled) PayrollJournalBatch exists for the run
Post-payroll raises Critical AccountingUnbalanced when any active journal batch for the run has TotalDebit <> TotalCredit
Post-payroll raises Critical DuplicatePayrollJournal when more than one active journal batch exists for the same PayrollRunId
Post-payroll raises Critical AccountingPayrollTotalMismatch when every active journal IS balanced (debit=credit) but the posted credit total does not equal the run's persisted Net total

Post-payroll raises Critical BrokenAccountingReversalLinkage for any PayrollJournalLineSource whose SourceType contains 'Reversal' but whose SourceId does not resolve to a PayrollReversal linked to this run (as OriginalPayrollRunId or ReversalRunId)

Post-payroll raises Critical BrokenAccountingAdjustmentLinkage for any PayrollJournalLineSource whose SourceType contains 'Adjustment' but whose SourceId does not resolve to any PayrollAdjustment row for the tenant

Post-payroll raises Warning MissingStatutorySource when persisted PayrollStatutoryResults exist for the run but zero PayrollStatutoryReturnSources exist, without ever recalculating a statutory rate/basis

When both statutory results and return sources exist, each StatutoryType (ProvidentFund/Esi/ProfessionalTax/IncomeTax) is compared to its own return-source total independently via a hard-coded alias map (PF/ESI/PT/TDS name fragments); a per-type mismatch raises a Critical {Type}StatutorySourceMismatch finding, and the aggregate StatutorySourceMismatch only fires as a fallback when no per-type finding already covered the discrepancy
An exact persisted PF/ESI/PT/TDS statutory-result-to-return-source match for every type raises zero statutory findings

AddSettlementSourceFindingAsync raises a Critical {Source}SourceMismatch (Reimbursement/Loan/VariablePay/Adjustment) whenever the sum of matching PayrollResultComponents.CalculatedAmount (matched by a case-insensitive CalculationSource substring) does not equal the sum of the corresponding settlement/repayment/application table for the run - including the case where persisted components exist but the settlement source is entirely missing

A component-vs-settlement comparison that nets to exactly zero on both sides (no persisted component AND no persisted settlement for that source) raises no finding - only a genuine non-zero mismatch is reported
Post-payroll raises Critical DuplicateReimbursementSettlement when 2+ ReimbursementSettlements for the run share the same non-null ReimbursementClaimLineId

Post-payroll raises Critical DuplicateVariablePaySettlement when 2+ VariablePaySettlements for the run share the same VariablePayAwardId, and Critical DuplicateLoanRecovery when 2+ LoanRepayments for the run share the same non-null LoanInstallmentId

Post-payroll raises Critical DuplicatePayrollAdjustmentApplication when 2+ PayrollAdjustmentApplications for the run share the same PayrollAdjustmentId, and Critical BrokenPayrollAdjustmentReversalLinkage when a PayrollAdjustment sourced from 'PayrollReversal' has no matching, non-Cancelled PayrollReversal linking its OriginalPayrollRunId to this run
Post-payroll raises Critical FinalSettlementSourceMismatch when the sum of a FinalSettlementCase's own lines (earnings positive, deductions negative) does not equal its persisted NetSettlement value
Post-payroll raises Critical DuplicateFinalSettlementSource when 2+ FinalSettlementLines for the same case share the same (SourceType, SourceId) pair

A persisted GratuityCalculation's FinalGratuityAmount is compared to the matching Gratuity-type/source-tagged FinalSettlementLine(s); a missing line raises Critical MissingFinalSettlementGratuity and an amount mismatch raises Critical FinalSettlementGratuityMismatch
A persisted LeaveEncashmentCalculation's GrossAmount is compared to the matching LeaveEncashment-type/source-tagged line; a missing line raises Critical MissingFinalSettlementLeaveEncashment

A persisted NoticeSettlementCalculation is routed to MissingFinalSettlementNoticePay or MissingFinalSettlementNoticeRecovery depending on its own Type (NoticePay vs. NoticeRecovery), each checked independently against the matching line

Reimbursement/Loan/VariablePay/Adjustment Final Settlement lines are cross-checked against their own already-verified persisted source id (ReimbursementSettlements/LoanRepayments/VariablePaySettlements/PayrollAdjustmentApplications); a line whose SourceId does not resolve raises Critical MissingFinalSettlement{Source}, and a resolved-but-unequal amount raises Critical FinalSettlement{Source}Mismatch, sign-adjusted for IsDeduction

A Final Settlement case composed of all 8 categories (gratuity, leave encashment, reimbursement, variable pay/bonus, notice pay, notice recovery, loan recovery, payroll adjustment) in one settlement, each with an exact matching persisted source, raises zero Final-Settlement-category findings

Final Settlement category matching is keyed by FinalSettlementLine.LineType first and falls back to a SourceType substring match, so a line tagged with an unexpected LineType but a matching SourceType string is still picked up by the persisted-category helper
GetReconciliationAsync returns a reconciliation by id together with all of its Findings, scoped to the caller's tenant, else NotFound
Regenerating the same PayrollRunId+ReconciliationType creates a new, higher-Version row rather than overwriting the prior one; all prior versions' rows and their findings remain queryable by id

TotalChecks/PassedChecks/WarningChecks/CriticalChecks/FailedChecks on the reconciliation row are derived counts (TotalChecks = max(1, evaluated-controls + 1); FailedChecks = CriticalChecks = count of Critical findings; WarningChecks = count of Warning findings; PassedChecks = TotalChecks - total findings) computed once at generation time, not live-recomputed on read

PayrollReconciliation.Status is always Generated at creation and is never transitioned to Acknowledged or Superseded by any code path, including after every one of its findings is Resolved or after a newer version is generated (see CR-297)
A GetReconciliationAsync call for an id that exists in the database but under a different tenant returns NotFound, not the other tenant's data or a generic error

GetFindingsAsync lists a run's PayrollReconciliationFindings across ALL of its reconciliation versions (joined via Reconciliation.PayrollRunId, not filtered to the latest version), paged and free-text searchable on ControlCode/Message
Findings are ordered by GeneratedAtUtc descending then Id ascending as a stable tiebreaker, independent of any SortBy value supplied
ActOnFindingAsync('acknowledge') transitions an Open finding to Acknowledged, stamping AcknowledgedAtUtc/AcknowledgedByUserId from the current clock/caller
ActOnFindingAsync('resolve') transitions a finding to Resolved, stamping ResolvedAtUtc/ResolvedByUserId and persisting the caller-supplied Note/Reference as ResolutionNote/ResolutionReference

ActOnFindingAsync('accept-exception') transitions a finding to AcceptedException with the same Note/Reference capture as resolve, but is gated by the SAME Payroll.Reconciliation.Resolve permission - there is no separate accept-exception permission

A finding already in a terminal state (Resolved or AcceptedException) rejects any further acknowledge/resolve/accept-exception call with Conflict; Acknowledged is NOT terminal - it can still be resolved or accepted-as-exception afterward
Permission: n/a (checked before the permission-gated action runs)

Functionality: An unrecognized action string (anything other than the exact literals 'acknowledge'/'resolve'/'accept-exception', case-insensitive) returns Invalid, without touching the finding row
ActOnFindingAsync requires the finding to resolve for the caller's tenant, else NotFound; there is no separate check that the finding's parent run itself still exists or is not Cancelled

PayrollAnomalyFlag rows are created ONLY as a side effect of GenerateReconciliationAsync(PostPayroll) finding NegativeNetPay or ZeroNetPay - there is no standalone anomaly-detection endpoint or background job

A duplicate NegativeNetPay/ZeroNetPay condition on a later regeneration does not create a second Open anomaly flag for the same employee/run - only when no Open flag of that type already exists is a new one added
GetExceptionsAsync lists PayrollAnomalyFlags TENANT-WIDE across every payroll run, joined to Employees for EmployeeCode - there is no payrollRunId query parameter to scope the register to one run

Free-text search on the exceptions register matches EmployeeCode or the anomaly's own Message only - there is no filter by AnomalyType, Severity, Status, or a date/period range anywhere on this endpoint
Exceptions are ordered by CreatedAtUtc descending then Id ascending, independent of any SortBy value supplied
An anomaly flag whose EmployeeId no longer resolves to any Employee row (or was never set, run-level anomalies) reports an empty EmployeeCode rather than erroring the whole list
ExportExceptionsAsync exports the same tenant-wide, Search-filterable set as a CSV (payroll-exceptions.csv, no run/date scoping), forcing PageSize to 50000 internally

12 of PayrollAnomalyType's 14 members (everything except NegativeNetPay/ZeroNetPay) are declared but have zero code path that ever constructs one - the exceptions register can never show them (see CR-298)

There is no exposed action anywhere to acknowledge, resolve, or otherwise change the Status of a PayrollAnomalyFlag row directly - AcknowledgedAtUtc/AcknowledgedByUserId/ResolutionNote are declared entity fields with no service method that ever sets them (Payroll.Exceptions.Manage is unused, see CR-292)
ListControlsAsync lists a tenant's PayrollVarianceControls, free-text searchable on Code/Name, ordered by Code ascending, paged
CreateControlAsync requires a non-blank Code and at least one of AbsoluteThreshold/PercentageThreshold, else Invalid

A duplicate (TenantId, Code, EffectiveFrom) triple is rejected with Conflict before insert, backed by a unique index of the same shape; the identical Code with a DIFFERENT EffectiveFrom is allowed (multiple effective-dated versions of the same control code)

UpdateControlAsync requires the control to exist in the tenant, else NotFound, and otherwise overwrites every field (Code/Name/Scope/Metric/thresholds/Severity/Action/AppliesToRunType/IsActive/EffectiveFrom/EffectiveTo) unconditionally - there is no partial/PATCH semantic

UpdateControlAsync does not increment or otherwise touch ConcurrencyVersion when applying changes, and does not re-check code/EffectiveFrom uniqueness against other rows, so a code collision can be introduced via update that CreateControlAsync itself would have rejected

A control may be created with any of the 8 PayrollControlScope values and any of the 9 PayrollControlMetric values with no server-side validation that the combination is ever actually evaluated by GenerateReconciliationAsync (see CR-293/CR-294)
IsActive=false and an EffectiveTo in the past both independently exclude a control from evaluation without deleting the row, and both can be flipped back via UpdateControlAsync
AppliesToRunType=null makes a control apply to every RunType (Regular/Supplementary/OffCycle); a non-null value restricts it to exactly that RunType
PayrollAnalyticsControlDto surfaces the control's own ConcurrencyVersion field to callers even though it is never enforced as an EF concurrency token and never incremented (see CR-290)

List/Create/Update of controls each independently require the caller's tenant context; a control created in one tenant is never visible or updatable from another tenant's context (including by direct id guess)
There is no delete/deactivate-only endpoint distinct from Update - the only way to stop a control from being evaluated is to Update it with IsActive=false or an EffectiveTo in the past
Every read endpoint under api/payroll/analytics (overview/summary/control-totals/departments/cost-centers/variance/components/findings + 4 CSV exports) requires Payroll.Analytics.View
analytics-controls List requires Payroll.Analytics.View while Create/Update require the separate Payroll.Analytics.Configure permission
Both pre- and post-payroll reconciliation generation require Payroll.Reconciliation.Generate; reading a reconciliation by id requires the separate Payroll.Reconciliation.View
acknowledge requires Payroll.Reconciliation.Acknowledge while resolve AND accept-exception both require Payroll.Reconciliation.Resolve (see F-PYA-079/CR pattern)
Both exceptions endpoints (list, export.csv) require Payroll.Exceptions.View; Payroll.Exceptions.Manage is granted by the seed data but gates no endpoint at all
A caller holding Payroll.Analytics.View but not Payroll.Analytics.Configure can list controls but receives Forbidden on Create/Update
A caller holding Payroll.Reconciliation.Acknowledge but not Payroll.Reconciliation.Resolve can acknowledge a finding but receives Forbidden on resolve/accept-exception for the same finding
A request with a well-formed but expired/absent bearer token receives Unauthorized (401) uniformly across all 22 endpoints in this module, before any permission or tenant check runs

A full grep of SeedData.cs's RolePermissionMap for all 8 Payroll.Analytics*/Reconciliation*/Exceptions* constants matches only the blanket DomainPermissions.All grant to SuperAdmin/TenantAdmin - no seeded HRAdmin/HRManager/SuperHR/Accounts/IT/Manager/Employee role holds any of them out of the box (see CR-291)
A custom role assembled with exactly one of the 8 Payroll.Analytics*/Reconciliation*/Exceptions* permissions can access exactly the endpoint(s) gated by that permission and no others in this module

The fallback authorization policy denies every endpoint in this module if its [HasPermission] attribute were ever removed - confirmed structurally (every action carries an explicit attribute; none are [AllowAnonymous])

Platform-admin bearer tokens (PlatformBearer/PlatformPermission) are a separate identity domain and cannot authorize any endpoint in this module, including a Platform SuperAdmin acting without a resolved tenant-scoped JWT
Every read/write in this module filters by the server-resolved TenantId from the caller's JWT/ShardContext, never from a client-supplied value

A payroll run id belonging to Tenant B, requested by a caller authenticated to Tenant A, returns NotFound/Unauthorized from EVERY overview/summary/control-totals/dimension/variance/component/findings/CSV-export endpoint - never Tenant B's data
A reconciliation id or finding id belonging to Tenant B, requested by Tenant A, returns NotFound from Get/Acknowledge/Resolve/Accept-exception - never Tenant B's row

A PayrollVarianceControl created under Tenant A is invisible to List/Update under Tenant B, and Tenant B may create its own control with the identical Code/EffectiveFrom Tenant A already used (the unique index is TenantId-scoped)
The exceptions register is tenant-scoped even though it is run-unscoped - Tenant A never sees Tenant B's PayrollAnomalyFlags rows regardless of search text

GetVarianceAsync/GetComponentVarianceAsync's default comparison-run lookup is itself tenant-filtered - a same-RunType run belonging to another tenant is never selected as the implicit comparison baseline

The unique (TenantId, PayrollRunId, ReconciliationType, Version) index guarantees that two concurrent GenerateReconciliationAsync calls for the same run/type cannot both persist the same version - the DB, not application logic, is the sole race guard, and the losing caller surfaces an unhandled DbUpdateException rather than a graceful Conflict

Every successful GenerateReconciliationAsync call inserts exactly one matching PayrollAnalyticsSnapshot row at the same DataVersion, so the reconciliation-row count and snapshot-row count for a run+type always stay equal even under a race

PayrollReconciliationFinding rows carry no concurrency token at all (not even the unenforced ConcurrencyVersion int that PayrollReconciliation/PayrollVarianceControl declare) - two concurrent ActOnFindingAsync calls against the SAME finding (e.g. acknowledge vs. resolve) never raise a conflict; the later SaveChangesAsync call silently overwrites the earlier one's Status/timestamps (see CR-290)

Two concurrent acknowledge calls against the same finding both report Succeeded=true (the terminal-state guard only rejects a call arriving after Resolved/AcceptedException, not after another Acknowledged) and leave one final, auditable Acknowledged state with the last writer's actor/timestamp

A PayrollVarianceControl Update racing a reconciliation Generate for the same tenant does not corrupt either row - exactly one control row and the expected reconciliation row(s) exist afterward, though which control values (pre- or post-update) the race's Generate actually evaluated is not guaranteed

A finding Resolve racing a same-run-type reconciliation regeneration preserves the resolution's Note/Reference/terminal status on the original finding row while the new version's own (separate) findings are generated independently - resolving version N never mutates version N+1's findings

A PayrollJournalBatch insert (accounting posting) racing a post-payroll reconciliation Generate for the same run leaves exactly one journal batch row and a reconciliation row reflecting a consistent (not partially-committed) read of whichever state actually committed first

Employee variance pages correctly over 500 employees across 2 payroll runs (page 1 and page 10 of 50 both return exactly 50 rows with TotalCount=500), with every row's GrossDelta reflecting the correct per-employee prior-vs-current difference

Department/CostCenter summaries over 500 employees split across 2 Departments/2 CostCenters each sum back exactly to the run's overall Gross/Deduction/Net control totals - no employee is double-counted or dropped across dimension groups
Component variance over 500 employees' components correctly sums a shared ComponentCode into one aggregate row rather than one row per employee

A requested PageSize above PagedQuery.MaxPageSize (100) is clamped/rejected consistently by the shared binding layer for every list endpoint in this module (Variance/Findings/Exceptions/ListControls), not by each service individually
A Page number beyond the last available page returns an empty Items array with the correct (unchanged) TotalCount, not an error

PayrollAnalyticsProviderAcceptance.RunAsync is the single shared helper both SqlServerPayrollAnalyticsIntegrationTests and MySqlPayrollAnalyticsIntegrationTests call - there is no provider-specific business-logic branch anywhere in PayrollAnalyticsService

The shared acceptance helper exercises control create, pre- and post-payroll generation, version-2 regeneration, finding list, acknowledge, resolve, run summary, control totals, department/cost-center summary, and all 4 CSV exports against a real disposable SQL Server and MySQL database in one pass, each run twice for same-database repeatability

Both provider migration chains (SQL Server 20260922050332 + 20260922081107; MySQL 20260922050406 + 20260922081130) create equivalent schemas for the 5 Analytics entities, and EF reports no pending model changes for either provider at authoring time

MySQL's app-managed binary(16) concurrency-token convention does not apply to this module's entities at all, since none of PayrollVarianceControl/PayrollReconciliation/PayrollReconciliationFinding/PayrollAnomalyFlag/PayrollAnalyticsSnapshot declare an EF concurrency token on either provider (reinforces CR-290 - the gap is provider-independent, not a MySQL-specific omission)
/payroll/analytics is registered in App.tsx behind RequirePermission(Permissions.payroll.analyticsView), rendering PayrollAnalyticsPage

PayrollAnalyticsPage reads its target run exclusively from a raw window.location ?runId= query-string parameter (not a route param, not a picker UI); with no runId present it renders a plain instructional paragraph instead of erroring

With a runId, the page renders a 7-tile summary grid (Employees/Gross/Deductions/Net pay/Open findings/Critical findings/Anomalies) sourced from getPayrollAnalyticsOverview - there is no variance table, no findings list, no reconciliation-generate button, and no export link on this page
A query failure (e.g. an invalid runId, or a 401/403/404 from the overview call) renders the raw error message via role=alert, with no retry action and no distinction drawn between 401/403/404/500

src/api/payrollAnalytics.ts wraps exactly 2 of the module's 22 backend endpoints (overview, employee variance) - getPayrollVariance is exported but never called from PayrollAnalyticsPage or any other page in this repository

generatePayrollReconciliation(runId, 'pre'|'post') is implemented in the API client but is never invoked by any page - there is no UI button anywhere that triggers pre/post reconciliation generation (see CR-296)

layout/navigation.ts has no entry linking to /payroll/analytics from any sidebar group; a permission-holding user can reach the page only by typing the URL (with a valid ?runId=) directly, since no other page in the frontend links to it either
FindingsCsv exports a run's findings (across all reconciliation versions, same source set as the JSON findings list) as a CSV with the documented 15-column shape, forcing PageSize to 50000 internally

All 5 CSV export actions (variance.csv/findings.csv/summary.csv/control-totals.csv/exceptions export.csv) return 400 BadRequest for ANY underlying failure - including NotFound and Unauthorized - rather than the status code the identical failure would map to on the JSON counterpart (404/401)
